diagnostic_approaches.name: MCAO diagnostic definition (≥50% central airway narrowing)
criteria_or_scoring: 50% or greater narrowing of the central airways
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: MCAO is defined as 50% or greater narrowing of the central airways, including trachea, mainstem bronchi, bronchus intermedius, and lobar bronchi

diagnostic_approaches.name: Anatomical classification of MCAO (intrinsic, extrinsic, mixed)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Classify MCAO by anatomy of airway compromise
criteria_or_scoring: Extrinsic: entirely extraluminal due to mass effect
Mixed: both intrinsic and extrinsic components
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Identifies pattern of obstruction (intrinsic, extrinsic, mixed)
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: MCAO can be classified based on the anatomy of airway compromise into intrinsic or endobronchial, extrinsic, and mixed (Fig. 1) [1].

diagnostic_approaches.name: Clinical history and physical examination
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Establish diagnosis of MCAO and assess severity/trajectory
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Comprehensive clinical history and physical exam
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Patients often present with dyspnea; stridor or unilateral wheeze on examination; positional aggravation with lying flat
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: The diagnosis of MCAO is established on the history, physical examination, and imaging [1, 4].

diagnostic_approaches.name: Chest X-ray
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Initial imaging; may suggest abnormalities but limited for MCAO
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: While chest X-rays may be readily available, the findings may be nonspecific as the airway anatomy is poorly defined [20].

diagnostic_approaches.name: Chest CT scan
limitations: May underestimate extent compared to bronchoscopy
may overestimate when mucus or blood masquerade as tissue obstruction
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: The computerized tomography (CT) of the chest remains the most reliable means of diagnosing and characterizing MCAO [4].

diagnostic_approaches.name: Assessment for patent distal airway (radiographic or bronchoscopic)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Predict likelihood of successful relief of MCAO
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Assess distal airway patency on imaging or bronchoscopy
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Indicator of successful relief; may portend more favorable bronchoscopic outcome
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Visualization of a patent distal airway either radiographically or bronchoscopically has been shown to be an indicator of successful relief of MCAO and may portend more favorable bronchoscopic outcome [19].

diagnostic_approaches.name: Duration of lobar atelectasis assessment
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Assess potential irreversibility of atelectatic lung
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Greater than four weeks may suggest the atelectatic lung is irredeemable
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Duration of lobar atelectasis of greater than four weeks may suggest the atelectatic lung is irredeemable [20].

diagnostic_approaches.name: Spirometry with flow-volume loop analysis
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Functional testing to identify pattern of airway obstruction
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Expiratory flattening: variable intrathoracic; inspiratory: variable extrathoracic; combined: fixed obstruction
limitations: May not be feasible in profound symptoms or acute respiratory failure
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: spirometry may show patterns of expiratory, inspiratory, or combined flow-volume loop flattening which have been associated with variable intrathoracic, variable extrathoracic, or fixed obstruction, respectively [4].

diagnostic_approaches.name: Mouth opening assessment (>3 finger breadths)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Inform the difficulty of endotracheal tube placement or rigid bronchoscopy
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: following components of examination can inform the difficulty of endotracheal tube placement or rigid bronchoscopy: 1. Mouth opening (normal >3 finger breadths) [36]

diagnostic_approaches.name: Dental assessment (teeth: loose, missing, or prominent)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Inform the difficulty of endotracheal tube placement or rigid bronchoscopy
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: following components of examination can inform the difficulty of endotracheal tube placement or rigid bronchoscopy: 2. Teeth, like loose, missing or prominent [36]

diagnostic_approaches.name: Modified Mallampati score
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Inform the difficulty of endotracheal tube placement or rigid bronchoscopy
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: following components of examination can inform the difficulty of endotracheal tube placement or rigid bronchoscopy: 3. Modified Mallampati score [37, 38]

diagnostic_approaches.name: Neck mobility assessment (>90°)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Inform the difficulty of endotracheal tube placement or rigid bronchoscopy
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: following components of examination can inform the difficulty of endotracheal tube placement or rigid bronchoscopy: 4. Neck mobility (Normal >90°) [36]

diagnostic_approaches.name: Thyromental distance assessment (>3 finger breadths)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Inform the difficulty of endotracheal tube placement or rigid bronchoscopy
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: following components of examination can inform the difficulty of endotracheal tube placement or rigid bronchoscopy: 5. Thyromental distance (normal >3 finger breadths) [36]

diagnostic_approaches.name: Surveillance bronchoscopy after airway stent placement
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Detect stent-related complications after stent insertion.
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Routine surveillance bronchoscopy within three months of stent insertion or when patients are symptomatic.
limitations: The evidence is unclear about the role of surveillance bronchoscopies after airway stent placement.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: compared routine surveillance bronchoscopy within three months of stent insertion to bronchoscopy when patients were symptomatic.

diagnostic_approaches.name: CT chest for stent surveillance and patency assessment
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Assess stent patency on surveillance imaging.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: For surveillance to assess stent patency.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: CT chest can be utilized for surveillance and assess stent patency [1, 60].

treatment_algorithms.title: Suggested algorithm for the management of malignant central airway obstruction
specific_recommendations: Surgical Management (for Surgical Candidate).
Debridement/Ablation of Endobronchial Tumor.
Stent Placement for Extrinsic Obstruction or Tumor Recurrence.
Possible Local Bronchoscopic Therapy (photodynamic therapy, brachytherapy, cryotherapy, or intratumoral chemotherapy injection).
Systemic Chemotherapy + External Beam Radiation.
decision_points_and_pathways: Non-surgical Candidate -> Debridement/Ablation of Endobronchial Tumor -> Stent Placement for Extrinsic Obstruction or Tumor Recurrence -> Possible Local Bronchoscopic Therapy -> Systemic Chemotherapy + External Beam Radiation.
treatment_algorithms.source_excerpt: Fig. 5 Suggested algorithm for the management of malignant central airway obstruction. *Local bronchoscopic therapy may include photodynamic therapy, brachytherapy, cryotherapy, or intratumoral chemotherapy injection.

clinical_guidelines.title: ACCP guideline: Rigid over flexible bronchoscopy for therapeutic interventions
specific_recommendations: Use rigid bronchoscopy over flexible bronchoscopy for therapeutic interventions in central airway obstruction.
Consider rigid bronchoscopy particularly for large and proximal central airway tumors.
Flexible bronchoscope might be adequate for distal and smaller airway lesions and is used as an adjunct with almost all rigid bronchoscopy cases.
Silicone stents can only be deployed through rigid bronchoscopes.
alternative_approaches: Flexible bronchoscopy for distal and smaller airway lesions (used as an adjunct in most rigid bronchoscopy cases).
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Therefore, the American College of Chest Physicians (ACCP) guidelines for management of central airway obstruction suggested rigid over ﬂexible bronchoscopy for therapeutic interventions [1].

clinical_guidelines.title: ACCP guideline: Anesthetic approach for therapeutic bronchoscopy
specific_recommendations: Use general anesthesia/deep sedation with paralytics for therapeutic bronchoscopy.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: The ACCP guidelines suggest the use of general anesthesia/deep sedation with paralytics for therapeutic bronchoscopy [1].

clinical_guidelines.title: ACCP guideline: Ventilator support during therapeutic bronchoscopy under general anesthesia
specific_recommendations: Use either jet ventilation or controlled/spontaneous assisted ventilation for therapeutic bronchoscopy under general anesthesia.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: The ACCP guidelines suggest the use of either jet or controlled/ spontaneous assisted ventilation for therapeutic bronchoscopy under general anesthesia [1].

clinical_guidelines.title: General management recommendations for MCAO
specific_recommendations: Therapeutic bronchoscopy under general anesthesia is the main approach to management.
Use multimodality therapeutic bronchoscopy to maximize procedural success.
Treat with definitive chemoradiation and/or surgery.
Adopt a multidisciplinary, patient-centric approach.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Patients with malignant central airway obstruction
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: The main approach to management is therapeutic bronchoscopy under general anesthesia. In addition, these patients should be treated with deﬁnitive chemoradiation and/or surgery.

clinical_guidelines.title: ACCP recommendations: Ablative therapies for airway patency in MCAO
specific_recommendations: Suggest tumor excision with ablative therapies to achieve airway patency.
decision_points_and_pathways: If tumor causes airway obstruction, use ablative therapies to excise/debulk to restore patency.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Patients with malignant central airway obstruction requiring restoration of airway patency.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: The ACCP guidelines suggest tumor excision with ablative therapies to achieve airway patency [1].

clinical_guidelines.title: ACCP recommendations: Consider local therapies with delayed effect for MCAO
specific_recommendations: Consider local therapies (e.g., PDT, brachytherapy, cryotherapy) that prevent tumor regrowth for MCAO management in select patients.
decision_points_and_pathways: If goal includes preventing tumor regrowth in MCAO, consider delayed-effect local therapies in select patients.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Select patients with MCAO where prevention of tumor regrowth is desired.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: ACCP guide- lines suggests to consider these “local therapies” that prevent tumor regrowth for MCAO management in select patients [1].

clinical_guidelines.title: ACCP recommendations: Airway stents for MCAO (indications and follow-up)
specific_recommendations: Consider airway stents in patients with extrinsic compression for palliation or while adjunct chemoradiation needs time to shrink the tumor.
In endobronchial CAO, use stents after tumor debridement in patients who failed initial chemoradiation or previous therapeutic bronchoscopies.
Carefully follow patients with airway stents and remove stents as soon as there is evidence of significant tumor regression.
Either routine surveillance or symptom-driven bronchoscopy is recommended after stent placement.
CT chest can be utilized for surveillance and assess stent patency.
decision_points_and_pathways: If extrinsic compression present -> consider stent for palliation or while awaiting chemoradiation effect.
If endobronchial CAO post-debridement with failed initial chemoradiation/previous bronchoscopies -> consider stent.
Post-stent placement -> choose routine surveillance bronchoscopy or symptom-driven approach; use CT chest to assess patency.
If significant tumor regression -> remove stent.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Patients with extrinsic compression or endobronchial CAO after debridement with failed initial chemoradiation/previous bronchoscopies.
clinical_guidelines.monitoring_requirements: Careful follow-up; routine or symptom-driven bronchoscopy; CT chest to assess stent patency; remove stent upon significant tumor regression.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: The airway stents should be considered in patients with extrinsic compression for palliation or while adjunct chemoradiation needs time to shrink the tumor [1].

clinical_guidelines.title: Safety recommendations for immediate-effect ablative therapies
specific_recommendations: Decrease the fraction of inhaled oxygen (FiO2) to ≤0.4 during ablative therapies.
Keep the active tip of ablative probes away from flammable devices like flexible bronchoscope or endotracheal tube.
decision_points_and_pathways: Before activating ablative device -> reduce FiO2 to ≤0.4 and ensure tip is away from flammable equipment.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Patients undergoing immediate-effect ablative therapies (e.g., APC, laser, electrocautery) for airway tumors.
clinical_guidelines.monitoring_requirements: Monitor oxygen concentration and device-tip positioning to reduce airway fire risk.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: decrease the fraction of inhaled oxygen (FiO2) to ≤0.4 and keep the active tip of the ablative probes away from flamma- ble devices… to decrease the risk of airway fire [1].

clinical_guidelines.title: Recommendations for EBRT in patients with MCAO and airway stents
clinical_guidelines.condition: Malignant Central Airway Obstruction (MCAO) receiving external beam radiation therapy (EBRT)
specific_recommendations: Carefully plan radiation for central airway tumors and adjust dose to minimize toxicity.
For high-risk patients, avoid concurrent chemotherapy and EBRT.
Remove airway stents as soon as feasible in high-risk settings.
decision_points_and_pathways: If central airway tumor planned for EBRT -> carefully plan and consider dose adjustment.
If patient is high-risk -> avoid concurrent chemo + EBRT and remove stent as soon as feasible.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Patients with central airway tumors, particularly those with airway stents and high risk for complications.
clinical_guidelines.contraindications_and_exceptions: Concurrent chemotherapy and EBRT should be avoided in high-risk patients.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: For high-risk patients, concurrent chemo- therapy and EBRT should be avoided, and stents should be removed as soon as feasible [61].

clinical_guidelines.title: ACCP and societal guidelines: Surgical management for airway or lung malignancy and carcinoid
clinical_guidelines.condition: Airway or lung malignancy; pulmonary carcinoid tumors
clinical_guidelines.source_organization: American College of Chest Physicians (ACCP) (and other societal guidelines)
specific_recommendations: Surgery should be considered as a definitive management in all patients who are surgical candidates.
For carcinoid tumors, surgical resection should follow if the patient is a suitable candidate.
If not fit for surgery, therapeutic bronchoscopy can be considered as the primary management option.
decision_points_and_pathways: If patient is a surgical candidate -> consider definitive surgical resection.
If carcinoid tumor and suitable candidate -> proceed with surgical resection.
If patient not fit for surgery -> consider therapeutic bronchoscopy as primary management.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Patients with airway or lung malignancy; patients with pulmonary carcinoid tumors who are surgical candidates or not fit for surgery.
clinical_guidelines.alternative_approaches: Therapeutic bronchoscopy as primary management when not fit for surgery.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Surgery should be considered as a definitive management in all patients who are surgical candidates [1].

clinical_guidelines.title: Photodynamic therapy (PDT) patient precautions
specific_recommendations: After PDT, patients need to avoid sunlight for up to eight weeks.
decision_points_and_pathways: Post-PDT -> counsel to avoid sunlight for up to eight weeks.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Patients receiving photodynamic therapy for airway lesions.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: PDT treatment is associated with photosensitivity and patients need to avoid sunlight for up to eight weeks after the treatment.

clinical_guidelines.title: Airway stent maintenance: mucociliary clearance therapy
clinical_guidelines.condition: Patients with airway stents for MCAO
specific_recommendations: Prescribe mucociliary clearance therapies like nebulized hypertonic saline or acetylcysteine to prevent mucus plugging of stents.
decision_points_and_pathways: After stent placement -> initiate mucociliary clearance therapy to prevent mucus plugging.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Patients with airway stents placed for malignant central airway obstruction.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: The patients should be prescribed mucociliary clearance therapies like nebulized hypertonic saline or acetylcysteine to prevent mucus plugging of the stents [11, 58].

clinical_cases.content: In a retrospective study of NSCLC patients with CAO, PDT with chemoradiation (n = 39) was compared to non-PDT ablation and chemoradiation (n = 558) [53]. Mean time for repeat intervention in PDT vs. non-PDT groups was 147 vs. 98 days (P = 0.20). All-cause mortality was lower in the PDT group.
